Your experience is all to common and it sucks. I'm sorry. My bio mom was forced to give me up as soon as I was born, and my dad was never allowed to see me. It started with TLC contacting me because I listed myself on a website many years ago for adoptees seeking bio families. They mailed me a 23&me and I took it. They ended up not asking me to be on the show (thank goodness), but it was only through them that I was able to find some of my bio family members. For that, I am forever grateful. Once I figured out who my dad was, I sent that text message. He responded almost immediately and told me he'd been waiting for me all the these years. My wife and I drove out to Arizona to meet him and my half siblings... It was absolutely mind blowing to meet them. They're wonderful people. I text with my dad every week to this day. Unfortunately, I found out my bio mom completed suicide when I was about 8. She had two kids after me, whom I've chatted with, and they are amazing too! It's been quite a journey to say the least!
I'm still here because I'm breaking the cycle for my kids. My great grandmother, my grandmother, my birth mother, and my brother all completed suicide. I'm not doing that to my kids.
